rawIdea: Let household members keep a shared shopping list that survives reloads and does not expose another household's items.

users.text: A signed-in household member manages their household's shopping list.

outcomes.text: An added item is still visible after a browser reload; another household cannot read or mutate it.

journeys.text: Sign in, open the household list, add an item, reload and verify the item remains.

requirements.text: A signed-in member can create and read household items persisted in the backend.
An item's name is nonempty after trimming; an empty list shows an explicit empty state.
A failed save retains the entered name and offers a retry without claiming success.
Authorization rejects anonymous and cross-household reads and mutations at the API boundary.
List controls work by keyboard, have accessible names and announce save errors; private household data is not submitted to model providers.

roles.text: Members can read and add only items belonging to their household; anonymous requests have no list access.

data.text: An item has an identifier, household owner, creator, trimmed name and creation time; household membership is the authorization boundary.

integrations.text: No third-party integration is needed for this slice.

constraints.text: Use synthetic household data during local preparation. Runtime, accounts, financial authority and deploy target must be selected separately before execution.

exclusions.text: Offline synchronization, invitations, billing and native mobile delivery are excluded from this first web slice.

assumptions.text: An offline mode might matter for grocery-store connectivity; this is a research proposal, not an accepted requirement.

openQuestions.text: Should a later slice support offline use?

ownerDecisions.text: Illustrative owner accepts this first web definition for design only.

acceptanceScenarios.given: A signed-in member with an empty household list and a real test backend
acceptanceScenarios.when: They add milk and reload the browser
acceptanceScenarios.then: Milk appears once in the same household list and the backend contains the household-owned item

acceptanceScenarios.text: Empty and invalid list states are explicit.
acceptanceScenarios.when: The member opens it and submits a whitespace-only name
acceptanceScenarios.then: The empty state remains visible and validation rejects the name without a persisted item

acceptanceScenarios.when: The member attempts to add bread then retries after recovery
acceptanceScenarios.then: The first attempt preserves bread and displays failure; the successful retry persists exactly one item

acceptanceScenarios.given: Two households and an anonymous client
acceptanceScenarios.when: The second household and anonymous client request the first household's list and attempt to mutate it
acceptanceScenarios.then: Every unauthorized request is rejected and the first household's data remains unchanged

acceptanceScenarios.given: A member using keyboard navigation and an accessibility inspector
acceptanceScenarios.when: They navigate list controls and encounter a controlled save failure
acceptanceScenarios.then: Controls have meaningful accessible names, the journey is operable without a mouse and the error is announced
